change.title: pr-7
change.description: scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes
change.author: Jeff Atwood

findings.title: Light-theme color changed from 30% to 70% lightness on `.a` in post replies
findings.body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new light-theme argument is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, and the dark argument is `$secondary 30%`. `dark-light-choose` returns its first argument for light themes (common/foundation/variables.scss:46-48), so bold reply-author links get much lighter on every light theme, which is a regression. The PR only claims to add dark-theme handling. The pair that preserves the light theme and mirrors it for dark is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.

findings.title: `.custom-message-length` light-theme color changed from 70% to 30%
findings.body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new call is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme result changes from a pale hint color to a much darker one. The matching desktop rule (desktop/modal.scss:94) correctly uses `70%` and `$secondary 30%`. The mobile one has the two values swapped, so mobile and desktop now differ. Use `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`.

findings.title: `h3` color changed from primary 20% to 50% in light theme
findings.body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new call uses `50%` for both `$primary` and `$secondary`, so the light-theme title color gets noticeably lighter. The matching desktop h3 (desktop/topic-post.scss:321) keeps `$primary 20%` and `$secondary 80%`. Use that pair here.

findings.title: Group member `.name` color changed from primary 30% to 50% in light theme
findings.body: The old value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new call uses 50% for both themes, so the light theme lightens and the name loses emphasis against the `.title` rule below it, which is also 50%. The light/dark pair that preserves the original is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`, which is what common/base/user.scss:119 and :124 use. The same mistake appears in mobile/user.scss:497.

findings.title: Group member `.name` color changed from primary 30% to 50% in light theme
findings.body: This is the same copy-paste error as desktop/user.scss:522. The original `$primary 30%` became `$primary 50%`/`$secondary 50%`, which lightens the light theme. Use `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.

summary: The change wraps `scale-color($primary, …)` colors in `dark-light-choose` with a mirrored `$secondary` lightness. Most of the 32 files do this correctly. Five lines break the pattern and change the light-theme color: desktop/topic-post.scss:291, mobile/modal.scss:102, mobile/topic-post.scss:182, desktop/user.scss:522 and mobile/user.scss:497. I did not check the dark-theme values against a rendered theme. I also did not review the other places the light-theme colors are overridden.
